_rules: frames-v7 aggregate: per-desktop snapshots keyed by desktop_id with replace semantics (a different boot always replaces; the same boot needs a greater seq); a snapshot is live while its socket is online, or for 15 s after an observed close, or for 90 s after it was received when the relay has observed nothing since it started; sums over live snapshots; the oldest amber by (since, desktop_id); the activity runs while amber > 0 and ends 60 s after it reaches 0; at most 4 pushes in any 60 s window, a held push sent at (4th most recent send + 60) with the aggregate as of then; priority 10 for start, end and an update whose amber or oldest.request_id changed, else 5.

events.note: the app posted its push-to-start token on launch
A connects: two sessions working, nothing amber, so no activity starts
B connects with CB-318 amber since t+3: the first amber starts the activity
iOS launched the app for the start and it posted the update token; nothing changed, so no update follows
A's orbweaver-site goes amber at t+9: amber 1 -> 2, priority 10; the oldest stays B's (3 < 9)
the prompt for R2 leaves A right after its activity frame, so the amber alert's counts already say 2
A's orbweaver finishes: working 2 -> 1, idle 0 -> 1, amber unchanged, priority 5
B's loginid-sdk-web finishes: fourth push inside the minute; the budget is now spent until t+65
CB-318 is answered at the desk and sdk-web starts working: amber 2 -> 1, but no token until t+65, so HELD
A's orbweaver starts working again while the hold stands; the hold's content is whatever is true at release, not this
a late copy of A's seq 3 from a replaced socket: activity_stale, nothing changes
B's socket drops; it counts for 15 more seconds
the hold releases at the 4th most recent send (t+5) + 60: one update with the aggregate as of t+65, priority 10 because amber and the oldest changed since the last push
B has been gone 15 s: it stops counting (machines 2 -> 1, working 2 -> 1), priority 5
B is back with a new boot and seq 1, accepted whatever the old seq was; machines 1 -> 2, priority 5
orbweaver-site answered on A: no amber anywhere, priority 10, and the end becomes due at t+140
sdk-web on B asks something the desk could not read (no tool, no command: Open on desk): the end is cancelled; the budget (65, 71, 75, 80) holds this until t+125
the held update goes with the state as of t+125
answered: amber 0 again, held until t+131 (71 + 60), end due 60 s after the aggregate reached zero, at t+190
the held update: amber 0, priority 10
no amber for 60 s: the end push, dismissal-date now
the relay restarts: snapshots survive in Postgres, sockets and the budget do not
after the restart nothing is observed about either socket: A's snapshot (received t+80) is 121 s old and outside the 90 s restart grace, B's (t+130) is 71 s old and inside it
A reconnects after its own silence timeout with a new boot: an amber, so a start goes to the start token; B still counts through the restart grace
B's restart grace ran out at t+220 and it never reconnected: machines 2 -> 1; the activity is only starting, so nothing can be sent
no update token within 30 s of the start: state none, and no start before t+535
still an amber on A, but the relay will not try another start until t+535

counts_budget._note: MEASURED, replacing CB-321's 'the slack covers counts': at the longest e the edge admits the slack is slack_bytes, not the size of counts, so an e longer than e_max_chars_with_counts loses to counts by the fallback (e is dropped, counts stay). A real sealed e (a title, a tool and a detail of at most 512 units) is a fraction of that. The relay's guard and these numbers are pinned against each other.

channel_requests.note: Channel mode (CB-323, the lead's decision of 10 Nov 2026), enabled by RELAY_ACTIVITY_CHANNELS: the per-activity update token never reaches the app after a push-to-start (measured on the simulator, and widely reported on devices), so updates and ends move to iOS 18 BROADCAST CHANNELS. One channel per phone, made by the relay. The start stays a push-to-start to the phone's token. With the setting off the relay behaves as before (the update-token lifecycle). Sources: developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/sending-channel-management-requests-to-apns, sending-broadcast-push-notification-requests-to-apns, setting-up-broadcast-push-notifications.

hosts.rules: Apple's send page says api.sandbox.push.apple.com / api.push.apple.com in its text and uses api-broadcast.sandbox.push.apple.com in its sample. MEASURED in the sandbox on 10 Nov 2026 with a scratch call: a channel was created (201) and a send to it answered 200 on BOTH hosts. The relay's send host is configuration (APNS_BROADCAST_SEND_HOST); the default is the text's, the ordinary push host. Production was not touched. Management is HTTP/2 to the manage host; both need TLS 1.2+ and the same provider token as every other push.

create.rules: Policy 0 (No Message Stored): a higher publishing budget, and every send MUST carry apns-expiration 0 (a nonzero value is rejected, 400 BadExpirationDate). The policy cannot be changed later. The channel id is random base64, returned in the apns-channel-id RESPONSE header with an empty body; the relay never assumes a size for it. At most 10,000 channels per app per environment; development and production channels are separate.

delete.rules: Irreversible. APNs may still deliver stored messages afterwards, which a no-storage channel has none of.

start.rules: A start carries aps["input-push-channel"] = the phone's channel id, a string, right after `attributes` and before `content-state`; everything else about the start is unchanged (the alert included). It still goes to the phone's push-to-start token: broadcast cannot start an activity. A device that does not run iOS 18 does not start it; the deployment target is 18.0. The system subscribes the activity to the channel itself, so the app does nothing new to receive.

send.rules: An update or an end goes to the channel, with the unchanged `aps` body (content-state, stale-date, dismissal-date; max_broadcast_payload_bytes). Priority is the same rule as before. The pacer is unchanged.

ChannelNotRegistered.relay: the channel is gone (deleted, or never existed in this environment): forget it (devices.activity_channel_id cleared), the state becomes none, and the next start makes a new channel

FeatureNotEnabled.relay: the Broadcast capability is off for the topic: logged, no channel is stored, and no start is sent (a start with no channel could not be updated)

other.relay: logged by status and reason only; a failed create retries after channel_retry_after_s; a failed send still counted against the pacer

channel_requests.lifecycle: Per phone, in channel mode. none -> when amber > 0 and the relay holds a push-to-start token: if the phone has no channel, create one (management); on failure no start is sent and the next try is no sooner than channel_retry_after_s; on success store it and send `start` carrying it, and the state is RUNNING at once (there is no starting state, no update-token wait, no start_abandoned). running -> every change of change_key is an `update` to the channel, and an `end` is due end_after_s after amber reaches zero, exactly as before. `ended` from the phone, with any activity_id (a phone has one activity), makes the state none and keeps the channel, so the next start reuses it. An update_token is still accepted and stored by POST /v1/activity and is never used. A send answered ChannelNotRegistered: see errors. Persistence: the channel id and a running flag are stored per phone, so a restart restores running (one update at the restart, priority 10, content unknown). The channel is deleted (management DELETE, best effort) when the phone has no link left (an unpair) and when its device row is purged; the stored id goes either way. A start the phone never acted on leaves the relay running until the end timer ends it, then the next start works.
